title: A Trendy Classroom Management Strategy You Should Never Use you-should-never-use/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Michael Linsin critiques a classroom management technique gaining traction in school districts: rather than directly addressing a misbehaving student, the teacher praises the well-behaved students around them in hopes the offender will change their behavior to gain the same praise. Linsin describes this as a manipulative and dishonest tactic, a close cousin of the 'caught being good' strategy, that offers the offending student no real feedback or opportunity to reflect on their misbehavior. He warns it trains the entire class toward extrinsic motivation and, over time, makes difficult students less likely to improve. As an alternative, Linsin recommends a straightforward classroom management plan that clearly communicates rules and consequences, applies them consistently to all students, and follows through—paired with genuine, achievement-based praise rather than manipulation.
points: A trending district-encouraged strategy has teachers praise well-behaved students near a misbehaving student instead of addressing the misbehavior directly.
Linsin labels this tactic manipulative and dishonest, comparing it to a magician's sleight of hand that offers no real feedback or accountability to the offending student.
The strategy risks training the entire class toward extrinsic, praise-seeking motivation rather than genuine behavioral change.
Over time it makes the offending student less likely to improve and can foster classroom-wide neediness and dependency.
The recommended alternative is a clear classroom management plan applied equally to all students, paired with honest, achievement-based praise and consistent follow-through.
quotes: It’s a close cousin of the “caught being good” strategy, which we also don’t recommend, but is far more damaging to the targeted student.
You would give the students within proximity of the misbehaving student an enthusiastic pat on the back for not misbehaving.
It’s the classroom management version of a magician’s sleight of hand. But it’s cruel and dishonest and doesn’t help the student actually change their behavior.
It will make difficult students less inclined to get back on track in the future and turn your classroom into a petri dish of neediness, dependency, and underachievement.
Have a classroom management plan that clearly lays out the rules and consequences of the class.
What they really need is your honesty. They need your truth and forgiveness. They need your accountability, your leadership, and your consistency.
